target_customer: Angel investors who want to collaborate on sourcing and evaluating startups, and the startups raising from them
problem: Angel investing is fragmented and inefficient for both angels and founders, with little shared sourcing, evaluation and mentoring.
business_model: Angel investing collaboration platform; revenue model not found

founders.name: Mike Palmer
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a computer scientist and physicist who worked on computational biology and machine learning at Stanford and as an angel investor.

founders.name: Brian Goler
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no bio.

competitors.name: AngelList
competitors.what: Online platform for startups and angels with Syndicates that let lead angels pool investor money
competitors.traction_then: Received an SEC no-action letter in 2013 for Syndicates and launched the Maiden Lane fund in March 2014
competitors.funding_then: Maiden Lane launched with more than 25 million dollars from investors

competitors.name: FundersClub
competitors.what: Online venture fund and syndicate platform for accredited investors
competitors.traction_then: Received a similar SEC no-action letter to AngelList in the same 2013 period

technical_complexity.rationale: A collaboration and deal flow web app is standard engineering; regulatory structure, not code, was the hard part.

defensibility.rationale: AngelList already had network effects and syndicates, and a new platform had no data or investor lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AngelList kept expanding syndicates and funds through 2014; no source shows it acted on Unicornly specifically.

market_need_then: Angel investing was growing with online platforms and 2013 SEC no-action letters made syndicates workable; no Unicornly specific demand evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: Used unicorn.ly (Libya .ly domain hack); the domain now redirects to a for-sale page.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand was found; the unicorn word was already common startup slang.

outcome_analysis: Unicornly was a two person angel investing platform in YC Winter 2014 that left almost no public trace: no launch coverage, funding announcement or post-mortem was found in several searches. The category was already occupied by AngelList and FundersClub, but no source states why Unicornly stopped, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are assigned.
notes: No company website listed on the YC page; unicorn.ly redirects to a domain for sale page. The AngelList Wikipedia page was used for 2013 and March 2014 facts and the page itself is undated. A directory (shyft.ai) lists a similarly named product that may or may not be the same company. Education not found. Exit type shutdown is inferred from YC status Inactive.
